draft3: Compare processes on a stated mixture of cases. Each overall rate describes the cases that process received; different mixtures can reverse the ranking of their group rates.
In this fictional example, A succeeds on 9/10 easy cases and 10/100 hard cases. B succeeds on 80/100 easy cases and 0/10 hard cases. A leads in both groups: 90% versus 80%, and 10% versus 0%.
B nevertheless leads overall: 80/110, about 73%, against A's 19/110, about 17%. B received mainly easy cases; A received mainly hard ones. Their totals weight the groups differently.

Give both processes the same easy-case share q, between zero and one. Their weighted observed rates become 0.1+0.8q for A and 0.8q for B. A leads by ten percentage points under every common mixture. At a 50/50 split, the comparison is 50% versus 40%. These weights specify a comparison scenario; they do not identify a population's composition.

This arithmetic does not establish the effect of switching a case from B to A. The counts specify neither an assignment mechanism nor both outcomes for the same case. The descriptive comparison holds under stated weights; a causal claim needs more information.

draft3: Sela put the return ticket beside her father's letter. The ticket named a route home. The letter said: Tell us where you are. Below the five words, the page was blank. After three weeks away, she could read them as a request for a place or a request to come back.

Her coastal map lay across the drawing board. Each inlet had its name, but the rooming house where she worked was too small to appear. Through the window she could see the harbor at the center of the sheet. The view supplied no further sentence from her father.

Sela took a second copy and marked the rooming house with a dot. She wrote the street beside it. Her first fold ran through the dot; she tried another. Then she put the map into an envelope and addressed it to her father. She could send this answer without claiming to have answered both questions.

The ticket went back into the drawer. The envelope waited by the door for the morning post. Sela returned to the northern edge of the first map, where her pencil lines stopped. She sharpened the pencil but added no coast beyond them. The space remained empty. The envelope remained in the room.
